correctness.rationale: Definitions coincide with Teh (2026) temporal JR on complete elections with horizon at least the electorate size: singleton cohesion forces one satisfaction, and one satisfaction for each voter suffices for group JR. From any per-round welfare maximum, a noncritical round avoids every uniquely satisfied voter, so switching its binary winner satisfies every initially unserved voter without making a previously served voter unserved. Critical-round counting gives 1<=d=u+c<=n/2 and welfare at least (ell-c)a+cn/2. Since an alternative has at least n-a supporters, the switch loses at most 2a-n; the increasing rational bound and cross-product ell*n*(d-1)-c*(n-2)*(n/2-d)>=0 establish the sharp ratio. Strictness for d>1 and for a<n-1 forces one fixed minority voter and exclusive polarization at equality for n>=3. Explicit witness attains the ratio. Exact-arithmetic verification exhausts 19,683 and 531,441 three-voter profiles and tests 1,000 deterministic four-voter profiles; these support but do not replace proof.

Prior static two-party FJR+ findings impose a strictly stronger property than JR and do not determine this optimum. value.rationale: Repeated yes/no decisions form a natural restricted temporal-voting domain in which fairness and aggregate approval welfare genuinely compete. The result determines a nontrivial exact price for every n and ell, improves the generic many-candidate approximation, and reveals why one-round repair always works, even with arbitrary time-varying approvals. The complete rigid classification of worst-case polarized electorates has clear structural interpretation and is not mere parametric substitution. No generalization beyond its assumptions is claimed.
